# Diagnostics reference

A [Developer Diagnostic](declaration-faults.md#developer-diagnostics) ends its banner with the identity of the rule it reports. Find that identity here to read the rule's headline and the explanation of why the rule exists. Each package lists its rules by identity.

## @loomcli/core

### @loomcli/core/argument-declared-twice

**Argument declared twice.** An action reads each argument under its name, so two arguments with one name leave one of them unreadable.

### @loomcli/core/arguments-beside-children

**Arguments beside children.** A Command's first bare token either names a child or fills an argument, so a Command that holds both cannot tell which one an operator meant.

### @loomcli/core/background-mark

**Invalid background mark.** One string global option may carry the operator's background choice. Core reads it from argv right after host capture, beside the color choice and before anything else prints, so it takes no short alias and no second source.

### @loomcli/core/broken-attach-hook

**Broken attach hook.** onCommandAttach receives each Command's declaration at graph build and returns it, or a value derived from it, synchronously and without throwing. Core builds the Command the hook returns, so a throw leaves it nothing to build.

### @loomcli/core/broken-destination

**Broken destination.** Core writes the run's output and its failure reports to the host streams run() captured. A stream that fails a write loses whatever followed it, so the run cannot succeed.

### @loomcli/core/broken-failure-encoder

**Broken failure encoder.** A failure encoder turns a failure's form into the text a machine reader parses, synchronously and without throwing. Core wrote its own text for the failure in the encoder's place.

### @loomcli/core/broken-failure-view

**Broken failure view.** A failure view turns a failure into the text the operator reads, synchronously and without throwing. Core wrote its own text for the failure in the view's place.

### @loomcli/core/broken-graph-hook

**Broken graph hook.** onGraphBuilt receives the frozen graph once per build and judges it: it returns nothing, and it rejects the graph only by throwing a DeclarationError. Any other throw is a defect in the hook.

### @loomcli/core/color-mark

**Invalid color mark.** One Boolean global option may carry the operator's color choice. Core reads it from argv right after host capture, before anything else prints, so it takes no short alias and no second source.

### @loomcli/core/command-attached-twice

**Command attached twice.** A Command value sits at one place in the tree, where its path, its help page, and its parent read it, so one value attached at two places would have two paths.

### @loomcli/core/command-without-action

**Nothing to run.** Routing ends at a Command that runs its action, or passes on to one of a group's children. A Command with neither leaves an invocation that reaches it nothing to run.

### @loomcli/core/declared-name

**Invalid declared name.** An action reads each argument and option under its name, and help and diagnostics print it. A leading "-" reads as an option, and whitespace or "=" splits the name where the parser reads it.

### @loomcli/core/env-delimiter

**Empty environment delimiter.** A multiple option's variable splits at each occurrence of its envDelimiter into the option's list, and an empty string occurs between every two characters, so it separates no item.

### @loomcli/core/extension-output

**Extension output not plain data.** Every projection, the manifest included, reads an extension's output as frozen plain data: strings, finite numbers, Booleans, null, arrays, and plain objects.

### @loomcli/core/failure-code

**Invalid failure code.** A failure's code tells a script or an agent which failure ended the run, where many failures share one exit code. A machine reader branches on the code, so it follows one grammar: words of lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens. A code outside it is rejected where a failure of the class is constructed.

### @loomcli/core/failure-encoder-taken

**Failure encoder taken.** A failed run writes its failure through the one encoder registered for the media type its selected view declares. Two encoders for one media type leave core no way to choose between them.

### @loomcli/core/foreign-graph

**Graph not from inspect().** Core reads a Command graph through the build inspect() rendered it from. A graph inspect() did not return, or one whose nodes do not match that build, leaves core no build to read, so the run stops rather than hand a plugin the wrong Command.

### @loomcli/core/foreign-throw

**Unhandled exception.** Core reports a value that an action, a middleware, a configuration source, a view, a translator, or a plugin's hook threw, and that no translator answered, as a defect, because only the author knows what it means. A distributed build shows the operator one generic message in its place.

### @loomcli/core/foreign-value

**Value from another copy of core.** Core reads a plugin, an extension value, a declared view, a view override, a translation, a failure encoding, and a provider through facts the copy of @loomcli/core that built it recorded. When two copies of @loomcli/core are installed, a value one copy built carries no facts the other copy can read.

### @loomcli/core/interaction-mark

**Invalid interaction mark.** One Boolean global option may turn questions off, so two options that carry the mark would each claim the decision for the run.

### @loomcli/core/invalid-default

**Default rejected.** Each run passes every declared default through its validator before it reads a token, because a default reaches the action as a validated value. A default the validator rejects would reach no action, whatever the operator supplies.

### @loomcli/core/invalid-extension-value

**Invalid extension value.** An extension value passes its descriptor's schema at the call that carries it, synchronously, so every plugin that reads it reads a value the schema accepted.

### @loomcli/core/invalid-implied

**Implied value rejected.** Each run passes every implied value through its validator before it reads a token, because a bare spelling supplies it to the action as a validated value. An implied value the validator rejects is the declaration at fault, whatever the operator supplies, so the run reports it whether or not a bare spelling was typed.

### @loomcli/core/invalid-release-facts

**Invalid release facts.** The build bakes the release facts into \_\_LOOM\_RELEASE\_\_: a build of source, development, or distributed, and an optional release group with a semantic version, a repository as owner/name, and an optional asset name. A malformed value leaves the build unknown, so core shows the author this diagnostic in every build.

### @loomcli/core/invalid-shutdown-timeout

**Invalid shutdown timeout.** After an ending signal, core gives the runs shutdown.timeout milliseconds to unwind and then ends the process. A timer waits a whole number of milliseconds from 0 through 2147483647, so the budget is one of those.

### @loomcli/core/missing-input-name

**Unknown missing input.** A missing input names a local option of the routed Command.

### @loomcli/core/name-shared-across-kinds

**Argument and option share a name.** An onCommandAttach hook adds inputs to a Command whose other inputs the plugin did not declare, so each name a hook declares stays apart from every argument and option in the Command's scope, whichever kind holds it. An author who gives an argument and an option one name does so knowingly, but a hook cannot see the Command's inputs, so a shared name there is an accident the author did not choose.

### @loomcli/core/next-misuse

**next() misused.** next() continues the middleware chain once, while the middleware that received it runs. A second call, or a call after the middleware returned, has no chain left to continue.

### @loomcli/core/option-declared-twice

**Option declared twice.** An action reads the global options and its Command's own options from one options object, each under its declared name, and the global options, the application's and every installed plugin's, share every Command's one table of spellings. Two options with one name in either leave one of them unreadable.

### @loomcli/core/option-group

**Invalid option group.** An option group relates already-declared local options. Its members must be distinct and its rules must permit those options to be used.

### @loomcli/core/optional-argument-last

**Required argument after optional.** Bare words fill the arguments in order, and an operator leaves out optional arguments from the end of the line. A required argument after an optional one would leave the parser unable to tell which of the two a lone bare word fills.

### @loomcli/core/plugin-installed-twice

**Plugin installed twice.** Core keys each plugin by its identity, and a plugin contributes its options, middleware, hooks, and views once, so a second installation would contribute each of them again.

### @loomcli/core/plugin-loader-failed

**Plugin loader failed.** Core loads a plugin's middleware or source module the first time a run reaches it, and the module owes its function as its default export.

### @loomcli/core/portable-name

**Name not portable.** An operator types the application name, each Command name, and each alias as a command at a shell prompt. A character outside the POSIX portable filename set needs quoting there, a leading "-" reads as an option, and a leading "." names a file a shell hides.

### @loomcli/core/provider-name-taken

**Provider name taken.** An action reads each provided value under its provider's name, so two different providers with one name among the providers a uses list reaches would leave one name for two values. The types reject two such providers whose types differ; core rejects two that share one type, such as two values one generic factory returns, where the list is declared.

### @loomcli/core/quiet-mark

**Invalid quiet mark.** One counted global option may lower the run's verbosity by one step. Core settles the verbosity right after graph build, before it reads the environment or configuration, so the marked option takes no second source.

### @loomcli/core/result-contract

**Result contract broken.** A Command that declares a result promises its consumer one value, or one sequence of rows, that its action emits once through out.results().

### @loomcli/core/rule-identity

**Invalid rule identity.** A rule's identity names the package that declares it and the rule inside it, so tooling keys on it and two packages never share one. It is an identity, a package name and any kebab-case subpath segments that name the part of the package that owns the rule, then a kebab-case rule name, joined by /.

### @loomcli/core/schema-converter-failed

**Schema converter failed.** Help, the manifest, and completion read what an input accepts from the JSON Schema its validator publishes. A converter that throws or returns anything but a plain object publishes no shape, so a distributed build reads the input's schema as null.

### @loomcli/core/sibling-name-taken

**Name taken by a sibling.** Every canonical name and alias under one parent routes one token to one child, so a name that two siblings share cannot route.

### @loomcli/core/slot-taken

**Slot already claimed.** A slot is a position exactly one plugin claims: the theme and the configuration source. A second claim would leave two plugins answering where core asks one.

### @loomcli/core/source-answers

**Invalid source answers.** A configuration source answers with a record that maps each option core requested to { value, label }, where the value has the raw type the option takes and the label is one line of prose, and an answer may add a directory, the absolute path of the folder holding the file the value came from. Core fills no option from any other answer.

### @loomcli/core/spelling-taken

**Spelling used twice.** The parser reads each spelling as one option, and a Command's own options share one invocation with the global options and every installed plugin's options. A spelling two options claim, a short alias, an alias, or a generated negative form included, would reach only one of them.

### @loomcli/core/stdin-claimed-twice

**Stdin claimed twice.** A Command has one stdin stream, so at most one local content input or stdin-only declaration claims it.

### @loomcli/core/two-package-copies

**Two copies of one package.** Core keys each extension and each declared view by its identity and compares it by reference. Two distinct objects under one identity mean two copies of the package that defines it are installed, and a value one copy made cannot be read through the other.

### @loomcli/core/validator-failed

**Validator failed.** Only an issue a validator returns states a validation verdict. A validator that throws, rejects, or returns anything but a Standard Schema result leaves core no verdict to report, so validation stops and the action does not run.

### @loomcli/core/variable-bound-twice

**Variable bound twice.** Within one invocation's scope a variable fills one option, so two options that bind it would both take the value an operator set for one of them.

### @loomcli/core/variadic-argument-last

**Variadic argument not last.** A variadic argument takes every positional token that remains, so an argument after it would never receive one.

### @loomcli/core/verbose-mark

**Invalid verbose mark.** One counted global option may raise the run's verbosity. Core settles the verbosity right after graph build, before it reads the environment or configuration, so the marked option takes no second source.

### @loomcli/core/view-selection

**Invalid view selection.** A middleware, or the caller of invoke(), selects one of the views the routed Command's result declares, by name, before the action runs. A Command that declares no result has no view to select, and a name its result does not declare has no view to render.

## @loomcli/plugins

### @loomcli/plugins/config/empty-file

**Configuration schema rejects an empty file.** A command-line application runs before its operator has written any configuration, so the configuration schema accepts an empty file. The plugin drops every value the schema rejects and validates again, and a schema that still reports an issue once every key is gone, such as a refinement that fails for an empty object, leaves the plugin no file to give the application.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/file-path

**Invalid configuration file path.** The configuration plugin looks for its file in the start directory, each of its ancestors, and the home directory, so file is a relative path whose segments each name a directory or a file.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/file-pattern

**Invalid configuration file pattern.** The configuration plugin chooses a file's parser by its extension, so file holds glob syntax only as the whole extension of its name: \* for any format the plugin reads, or a brace list of json, jsonc, toml, yaml, and yml, tried in the order listed.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/link-path

**Option linked to a path the configuration schema does not hold.** An option linked with configInput takes the value the configuration file holds at its path, and the configuration schema describes the whole file. A path whose keys the schema does not describe means the shape of the file and the option disagree, and the check catches a typo or a stale link at build time.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/link-type

**Option linked to a value it cannot take.** An option linked with configInput takes a string or a number, a Boolean, a whole number, or an array, by its type. A path whose configuration schema holds no value of that kind can never fill the option, so the link is a mistake that only the assembled application reveals.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/root-name

**Invalid configuration root marker.** The configuration plugin's project walk checks each directory it looks in for an entry of each root marker's name, so a marker names one entry: it is nonempty, holds no slash or backslash, and is neither . nor ..

### @loomcli/plugins/config/root-without-project

**Configuration root marker without the project scope.** A root marker bounds the project walk, and a scopes list without project reads the home file and the user file alone, so the marker would bound nothing and its setting would say something the lookup never does.

### @loomcli/plugins/config/variable-name

**Invalid configuration variable name.** The configuration plugin reads the variable that env names from the run's environment, and an environment variable's name is a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits, or underscores, so a name of another form can never hold a value.

### @loomcli/plugins/dotenv/variable-name

**Invalid dotenv variable name.** The dotenv plugin compares each name an only or except list holds with the names the assignments in the dotenv files give, and an assignment names a variable with a letter or underscore followed by letters, digits, or underscores. A listed name of another form never matches, so the list would not do what it says.

### @loomcli/plugins/manifest/failure-code-conflict

**Failure code conflict.** The manifest lists each failure code once for the whole application, with one exit code and one meaning, so a consumer reads one contract for each code. Two declarations of one code that disagree leave it no single entry to list.

### @loomcli/plugins/manpage/page-name-taken

**Man page name taken.** The manpage plugin writes one page for each Command an operator can find, named by the application name and the Command's path joined with hyphens, so a Command named with a hyphen can give the name of a child's page, and one page would replace the other.

### @loomcli/plugins/mcp/property-name-taken

**MCP property name taken.** An MCP tool takes its arguments and options as one object keyed by declared name, so an argument and an option that share a name leave the client no way to supply each one.

### @loomcli/plugins/mcp/required-input-excluded

**Required MCP input excluded.** An excluded option is off its Command's MCP tool, and a tool call reads no source for it, so a required option that is excluded, a one-required group whose every member is excluded, and a required-together group that excludes some of its members leave calls of the tool missing a value the Command needs.

### @loomcli/plugins/mcp/tool-name-taken

**MCP tool name taken.** An MCP client calls a tool by its name: the Command path joined with underscores, or the application name for the root, with each hyphen written as an underscore. Two Commands that give one name leave the client no way to call either one.

### @loomcli/plugins/mcp/tool-without-action

**MCP tool without an action.** An MCP tool call runs the Command's action, so a Command with no action, such as a group, has nothing to run when a client calls it.

### @loomcli/plugins/self-update/settings

**Invalid self-update setting.** The self-update plugin reads the variable that notices.env names from the environment, as an input binds one, and turns update notices off when it is set and not empty, so env is a variable name: letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit.

### @loomcli/plugins/service/run-unrouted

**Service run words do not route.** The service unit runs the application with the words in run, so they name a Command that has an action, with its options and arguments, as the application's command line takes them. Words that route nowhere would leave the manager restarting a process that fails at once.

### @loomcli/plugins/service/settings

**Invalid service setting.** The service plugin names its unit by label: the systemd unit is \<label\>.service and the launchd agent's Label is the label. So label is a reverse-DNS name of two or more segments of letters, digits, and hyphens, each opening with a letter or digit, 247 characters at most, which keeps the unit name within systemd's 255 characters.

### @loomcli/plugins/skills/files

**Invalid skill files.** The skills plugin writes each skill as one folder in the operator's agent folders, so each file's path is relative to that folder, with no .. part that would write outside it, and the list holds the skill's SKILL.md, the file every agent reads first, and no listed skill holds a name the skills folder holds.

### @loomcli/plugins/skills/folder

**Unreadable skills folder.** The skills plugin installs each directory of the folder its folder setting names as one skill named by the directory, so the folder exists, holds a skill unless the application lists its skills, each skill directory's name is a skill name, and each entry inside a skill is a file, a link to a file, or a folder, never a link to a folder. A relative folder resolves against the application module, which only loom build knows, so a run loom build did not make reads the folder through a URL or an absolute path, and an artifact loom build made reads the copy it carries.

### @loomcli/plugins/skills/settings

**Invalid skills setting.** The skills plugin installs each skill as one folder, named by the skill's name, where an agent reads skills, so the settings name a folder of skills, a file URL or a nonempty path, or a list of skills, each name follows the Agent Skills grammar, lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, 64 characters at most, and no two skills hold one name.

### @loomcli/plugins/version/postfix

**Invalid version postfix.** The version plugin prints the postfix after the version on its one line, so the postfix holds a character other than whitespace and no line terminator.

## @loomcli/validators

### @loomcli/validators/bound-value

**Invalid bound.** A bound limits the values or the length a validator accepts, and the published schema carries it, so it is a value the schema can hold: a finite number for integer() and number(), a whole number of 0 or more for text()'s lengths, and a duration in the operator's grammar for duration().

### @loomcli/validators/bounds-order

**Bounds out of order.** A validator accepts what lies between its lower and its upper bound, both inclusive, so a lower bound above the upper one would reject every token.

### @loomcli/validators/context-outside-run

**Context outside a run.** Core attaches the validation context to each call it makes to a validator. A call from anywhere else, such as a unit test, carries none, so a validator that reads it runs inside an Application run, or a test passes it the options validationOptions builds.

### @loomcli/validators/input-schema

**Invalid input schema.** createValidator() publishes its input schema as draft 2020-12 JSON Schema and adds the $schema dialect itself, so inputSchema holds no $schema of its own.

### @loomcli/validators/invalid-pattern

**Invalid pattern.** text() publishes its pattern in the JSON Schema it serves, which reads a pattern under the u flag alone, so the pattern is a regular expression that compiles under u and carries no other flag.

### @loomcli/validators/issue-code-name

**Invalid issue code.** An issue code names the package that declares it and the one sentence it prints, so a view rewords that sentence by its code. It is a package name, any kebab-case subpath segments, and a kebab-case rule name, joined by /.

### @loomcli/validators/issue-parameters

**Issue parameters rejected.** An issue carries parameters its code's schema accepts, so every view that reads them through read() gets the shape the code declares.

### @loomcli/validators/one-of-values

**Invalid oneOf values.** oneOf() accepts a token equal to one of its values, and help, completion, and the published schema offer each value as a choice, and a JSON Schema enum lists each value once, so each value is distinct.

### @loomcli/validators/time-zone

**Invalid time zone.** dateTime() reads a token with no offset in the time zone it names, so the name is an IANA time zone the runtime knows, such as America/New\_York.

### @loomcli/validators/url-protocols

**Invalid url protocols.** url() accepts a URL whose scheme the list names and publishes the list as a pattern, so it holds at least one scheme name: a letter followed by letters, digits, +, -, or ., with no trailing colon.

## @loomcli/prompts

### @loomcli/prompts/link

**Invalid question.** A question asks in one line of prose and links one local option of the routed Command, of the kind the question accepts, and a select question offers at least one choice.

## @loomcli/loom

### @loomcli/loom/application-load-failed

**Application failed to load.** loom imports the application module to learn what it declares, loom init how the entry imports its Application and loom build the skills folder skills() names, and the module threw while it loaded, so the command could not finish.
